name: Quenby Fair Share Health Cover Act

source_sentences: The Act requires employers with 50 or more FTE to either offer each employee averaging 30 or more hours a week (130 hours in a month), from the first of the month after 60 days of employment, a plan meeting K2 with an employer contribution of at least 70% of the employee-only premium; or pay $250 a month ($3,000 a year) to the Department of Revenue for each such employee not so offered.
An employee who is offered and declines counts as offered.
Public employers and employees averaging under 30 hours are exempt.
Firms under common control are counted together.
Agency workers count for the agency.
No firm pays more than $300,000 a year under K1 (reached at 100 uncovered employees).
Employers report each employee's offer status on quarterly withholding returns; the charge is assessed with them.
Charges are paid into the general fund.
A new appropriation of $4.1 million a year from the general fund pays for 32 staff.
A plan counts under K1 only if it covers hospital, physician, prescription and maternity care, with a deductible no higher than $2,500, on a list kept by the Department of Insurance.
The standard binds insurers and self-insured employers.
The Department of Insurance certifies plans under K2.

unclear.text: The Act defines a seasonal worker (employed no more than 120 days in a calendar year in work that recurs at the same season) but does not say whether seasonal workers count toward the 50.
readings: U1-a: they count by their hours, like any other employee
U1-b: they are left out of the count

context: A state insurance department survey found that, of those 1.15 million, about 79% (910,000) are already offered a plan that meets the Act's benefit standard with an employer share of at least 70%; about 9% (105,000) are offered a plan that falls short on benefits or on the employer's share; and about 12% (135,000) are offered nothing.
Quenby's minimum wage is $14.00 an hour, indexed to prices; about 11% of private employees earn at or near it, mostly in retail, food service, cleaning, security and care.
